title: ExtractionBatch
description: Output of one extraction pass over a single communication window. Extraction is board-blind: it never references task ids and never decides anything. It only reports typed signals with evidence.

batch_id.description: Deterministic: sha256 of (window.source_ref + window.time_start + window.time_end + extractor.prompt_version). Re-running the same window with the same extractor produces the same batch_id, making re-runs idempotent.

extractor.description: Versioning for eval and regression. When rejection rates move, you need to know which model/prompt produced the signals.

source_ref.description: Graph resource id of the container: channel id, chat id, conversation id, onlineMeeting id, or driveItem id.

signal_id.description: Deterministic: sha256 of (batch_id + type + primary evidence resource_id + span). Stable across re-runs so downstream dedup is trivial.

type.description: proposal = a task someone floated but nobody committed to. completion_claim is separate from status_update because 'done' claims deserve stricter reconciliation (they close things).

title.description: Normalized short imperative, e.g. 'Migrate readmission model to Fargate'. Written by the extractor, not quoted from source.

author_ref.description: Who MADE this claim: the speaker of the primary cited evidence, resolved through the directory. Not part of signal_id, so adding it changed no existing id. Distinct from owner_candidates, which is who the work is FOR -- 'Priya said Dev finished it' has author Priya and owner Dev, and that difference is exactly what the corroboration rule means by independent speakers.

owner_candidates.description: Who this signal appears to belong to. Multiple candidates allowed; reconciliation resolves. Empty array = extractor could not attribute.

person_ref.description: AAD object id (preferred) or UPN. Never a display name — names are ambiguous.

basis.description: explicit_assignment: 'Alex, can you take X'. self_reference: 'I'll handle X'. inferred: everything weaker.

status_signal.description: What the communication implies about state. Null when the signal carries no state information (e.g. a pure deadline mention).

date.description: Resolved absolute date. Null if the extractor could not resolve the relative phrase; reconciliation may resolve it against the message timestamp.

raw_text.description: The phrase as spoken, e.g. 'end of next sprint'. Kept because date resolution of relative phrases is a top rejection cause and users need to see what the model heard.

blocking_party_ref.description: AAD object id of person/team the blocker waits on, if stated.

evidence.description: Mandatory. A signal with no evidence is invalid by construction.

EvidenceRef.description: A pointer, never a copy. Content is fetched at render time under the *viewer's* Graph permissions, so evidence display inherits permission trimming and retention policy instead of leaking copied text out of the compliance boundary.

resource_id.description: Graph id of the message/utterance/insight, addressable for later fetch.

span.description: Optional character offsets within the resource body, for highlight rendering.

content_hash.description: sha256 of the evidence text at extraction time. If the fetched content no longer matches (edited/deleted message), the UI flags the evidence as changed rather than silently showing different text.
